newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE grains down on sterling, Glickman comments.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE grains down on sterling, Glickman comments.

text.p: LIFFE grain futures ended easier, but off earlier lows.

A warning by US agriculture secretary Dan Glickman to the EU on export subsidies combined with sterling's strength to push futures to lows during the morning, traders said. There was a partial recovery later as sterling came off its highs.
Most active May dominated wheat volume with 407 of a total 653 lots traded. It last changed hands at 97.20 stg, down 0.40 stg, having seen a low of 96.75 stg.
Glickman on Monday repeated earlier statements that he is prepared to restart the U.S. agricultural subsidy program if necessary to fight European sales practices.

Speaking at the Agriculture Department's annual Agricultural Outlook Forum, Glickman said, "In our '98 budget, I've asked for full funding of our Export Enhancement Program ... That's my big stick, and I'm prepared to use it if that's necessary to protect our producers from unfair competition."
Barley also came down, with November most active. It last traded 0.35 stg lower at 93.00 stg.
